speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; I need to ask a few questions to determine the cause. REQUEST TEST: ECG to check for heart issues. REQUEST TEST: Troponin levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the ECG and Troponin results; since your heart appears normal, we need to determine if your chest pain and vomiting are gastrointestinal or neurological in origin. Does your chest pain radiate to your jaw or left arm, and do you have a history of migraines with visual disturbances before these symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallory-Weiss Syndrome

Based on the history of forceful retching and choking followed by chest pain, I am requesting an upper endoscopy (EGD) to visualize a mucosal tear. REQUEST TEST: EGD. Please also confirm if you have noticed any bright red blood or "coffee-ground" material in your vomit.
